title: Jericho's Walls May Be 900 Years Too Old
author: QUILL
notes: Dating contested; Garstang, Kenyon, Wood are claims. 900 = 2300 BC minus 1400 BC. Not-proven line in beat 9.

beats.text: Jericho's walls may be 900 years too old.
beats.source: claim by Kathleen Kenyon (c. 2300 BC vs c. 1400 BC)

beats.text: That's the gap between two digs, and a lab test breaks the tie.
Joshua 6: seven days of marching, and the wall falls down flat.
In the 1930s, John Garstang finds collapsed, burned walls and dates them near 1400 BC.
beats.say: In the nineteen thirties, John GAR-stang finds collapsed, burned walls and dates them near fourteen hundred B C.
beats.label: GARSTANG: C. 1400 BC

beats.text: But in the 1950s, Kathleen Kenyon re-digs it and disagrees.
beats.say: But in the nineteen fifties, Kathleen KEN-yon re-digs it and disagrees.

beats.text: Her walls are far older: about 2300 BC.
beats.say: Her walls are far older: about twenty-three hundred B C.

beats.text: In 1990, Bryant Wood argued pottery and scarabs fit 1400 BC.
beats.say: In nineteen ninety, Bryant Wood argued pottery and SCARE-abs fit fourteen hundred B C.
beats.label: WOOD: C. 1400 BC

beats.text: The lab verdict: radiocarbon on burned grain leans toward Kenyon.
beats.say: The lab verdict: radiocarbon on burned grain leans toward KEN-yon.

beats.text: Not proven: that these walls fell for Joshua.
Jericho, 250 metres below sea level: one mound, three verdicts.
Jericho's walls may be 900 years too old. Did they fall for Joshua, or earlier?

youtube.description:
Garstang, Kenyon and Bryant Wood read the same mound three ways, and radiocarbon leans toward the older date.
Whether these walls fell for Joshua is not proven; the dating is still contested.
